apt_groups.name: APT28
apt_groups.description: APT28 is a threat group attributed to Russia's General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 85th Main Special Service Center (GTsSS) military unit 26165. Active since at least 2004, they primarily target government, military, and security organizations.

apt_groups.name: APT29
apt_groups.description: APT29 is attributed to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR). Known for sophisticated supply chain attacks and cloud exploitation. Responsible for the SolarWinds compromise in 2020.

apt_groups.name: APT1
apt_groups.description: APT1 is a Chinese cyber espionage group attributed to the PLA's Unit 61398. One of the first APT groups publicly exposed, known for large-scale intellectual property theft from Western organizations.

apt_groups.name: APT10
apt_groups.description: APT10 is a Chinese cyber espionage group associated with the Ministry of State Security (MSS). Known for targeting managed IT service providers to gain access to their clients' networks (Operation Cloud Hopper).

apt_groups.name: APT41
apt_groups.description: APT41 is a dual espionage and financially motivated threat group attributed to China. Uniquely conducts both state-sponsored cyber espionage and financially motivated intrusions, including supply chain compromises and ransomware.

apt_groups.name: Lazarus Group
apt_groups.description: Lazarus Group is attributed to North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau. Known for both espionage and financially motivated attacks including the Sony Pictures hack, WannaCry ransomware, and large-scale cryptocurrency theft.

apt_groups.name: Kimsuky
apt_groups.description: Kimsuky is a North Korean threat group focused on intelligence collection targeting South Korean government, think tanks, and experts on Korean peninsula affairs. Known for social engineering and credential theft campaigns.

apt_groups.name: APT33
apt_groups.description: APT33 is an Iranian threat group targeting aerospace, energy, and petrochemical sectors. Known for destructive attacks using wiper malware and links to the Shamoon attacks.

apt_groups.name: APT34
apt_groups.description: APT34 is an Iranian threat group conducting cyber espionage primarily in the Middle East. Targets government, financial, energy, and telecommunications sectors using custom tools and social engineering.

apt_groups.name: APT35
apt_groups.description: APT35 is an Iranian threat group associated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Known for targeting activists, journalists, and government officials through elaborate social engineering campaigns.

apt_groups.name: Turla
apt_groups.description: Turla is a Russian threat group attributed to the FSB's Center 16. One of the most sophisticated APT groups, known for satellite-based C2, hijacking other APT group infrastructure, and targeting government and diplomatic entities.

apt_groups.name: Sandworm
apt_groups.description: Sandworm is attributed to Russia's GRU Unit 74455. Known for the most destructive cyber attacks in history including NotPetya, BlackEnergy attacks on Ukrainian power grid, and targeting the 2018 Olympics.

apt_groups.name: APT32
apt_groups.description: APT32 is a Vietnamese threat group targeting foreign corporations with interest in Vietnam's manufacturing, hospitality, and technology sectors, as well as foreign governments and dissidents.

apt_groups.name: SideWinder
apt_groups.description: SideWinder is an Indian threat group primarily targeting Pakistan and Chinese military and government entities. Known for high-volume spearphishing campaigns with rapid exploitation of vulnerabilities.

apt_groups.name: MuddyWater
apt_groups.description: MuddyWater is an Iranian threat group associated with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Targets telecommunications, government, and energy sectors across the Middle East and surrounding regions.

apt_groups.name: Gamaredon
apt_groups.description: Gamaredon is a Russian threat group attributed to the FSB's 18th Center operating from Crimea. Highly active in targeting Ukrainian government entities with high-volume, low-sophistication but persistent attacks.

apt_groups.name: Equation Group
apt_groups.description: Equation Group is widely attributed to the NSA's Tailored Access Operations (TAO). Known as one of the most technically sophisticated threat groups, operating a module framework that can reprogram hard drive firmware.

apt_groups.name: APT37
apt_groups.description: APT37 is a North Korean threat group targeting South Korean public and private sectors, with expanding operations against Japan, Vietnam, and the Middle East. Known for zero-day usage and diverse malware arsenal.

apt_groups.name: APT40
apt_groups.description: APT40 is a Chinese state-sponsored group attributed to the MSS Hainan State Security Department. Targets maritime industries, defense, technology, and government entities, particularly in the South China Sea region.

apt_groups.name: Mustang Panda
apt_groups.description: Mustang Panda is a Chinese threat group focused on targeting government, non-profit, and religious organizations across Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Americas using PlugX and custom tools.

apt_groups.name: Bitter
apt_groups.description: Bitter is a South Asian threat group primarily targeting Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Chinese government and energy sectors through spearphishing campaigns and mobile malware.

apt_groups.name: TA505
apt_groups.description: TA505 is a financially motivated threat group responsible for massive spam campaigns and distributing Dridex, Locky ransomware, and later Clop ransomware. Known for operating at enormous scale.

apt_groups.name: Patchwork
apt_groups.description: Patchwork is an Indian threat group known for copy-pasting code from various open-source tools and public exploits. Targets diplomatic and government entities primarily in Pakistan and China.

metadata.source: QiAnxin Threat Intelligence Center - APT Encyclopedia
